heartbeat.title: Ownership language beats waiting language
heartbeat.body_html: The most transferable result this month came from framing the product as already the customer's. Subject lines and copy built on near-ownership language, phrases like "basically yours", won across abandoned cart and site abandonment (tests 25, 37, 45), outperforming "still waiting" and passive possession framing. The lesson carries beyond one flow: reducing the psychological distance between browsing and owning lifts conversion at every late-funnel touch. We are rolling this framing into more sequences, and because winners are banked and losers cost nothing, each confirmed result compounds into the next month's baseline.

narrative.html: Flows earned 687,104 AUD, up 7.1% on last month, and accounted for 25.9% of total store revenue. This is the channel we manage most closely, and it continues to carry roughly a quarter of the store on its own.

Flow revenue per email delivered came in at 0.445 AUD, down from 0.611 AUD last month. Total flow revenue still rose, so the softer per-email figure reflects wider sends rather than weaker flows; we are watching send volume against yield to keep both moving together.

Flows remain the most efficient per-email channel we run. Flows earn 0.445 AUD per email versus 0.048 AUD from campaigns, about 9.3x more, and made up 76% of email revenue. Campaigns are the second lever we also run, with 26 sent this month adding reach that flows alone cannot.

Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.534% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.013%. Healthy list hygiene is what lets us keep testing and sending at volume without eroding inbox placement.

heartbeat.title: Name the behaviour, drop the cleverness
heartbeat.body_html:
The clearest signal from July's winning subject-line tests is that this healthcare audience rewards clarity over intrigue. Versions that named the subscriber and mirrored what they actually did, such as "you left some good ones behind", the plain "bumped your discount", the specific "6 pockets" claim, and peer validation like "other nurses picked these too", beat the punnier, more oblique controls again and again.

The transferable rule: lead with direct, personalised, behaviour-anchored language before the open, and save personality for inside the email. Each of these wins is now the permanent control it will be tested against next month, which is how the program compounds regardless of any single month's win rate.

narrative.html: Flows earned 650,521 AUD, up 2.5% on June. That is 25.7% of every dollar the store took this month, right in line with where this account has sat all year. This is the revenue that arrives on its own, triggered by customer behaviour, with no send required.

Flow revenue per email delivered eased to 0.619 AUD from 0.740. Total flow revenue still grew, so this reflects more emails reaching more people rather than weaker performance, but we are watching per-email yield and will keep the design and copy tests pointed at it.

Campaigns are the second lever we run, and the efficiency gap is clear. Across 20 campaigns sent, flows earned 0.619 AUD per email against 0.062 AUD for campaigns, so flows return 10.0x per email and hold 76% of total email revenue. Campaigns do the reach and timing work that flows cannot, while flows remain the most efficient per-email channel we run.

Deliverability stayed clean while we tested hard. Unsubscribes ran at 0.603% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.019%, both comfortably in safe territory, and we concluded 43 A/B tests this month with 20 winners banked.

heartbeat.title: Put the cost of doing nothing in the envelope
heartbeat.body_html:
The clearest pattern across this month's winners was in the subject and preview line. When we made the consequence of inaction explicit before the open, subscribers responded. The Back In Stock winner promoted the email's own closing warning ("gone again = gone for good") to the envelope, Abandoned Checkout won by naming that someone else might grab your size, and Abandoned Browse won by framing the offer as something the reader had earned.

Alongside that, language native to the audience beat templated phrasing: the Replenishment "last shift" healthcare pun outperformed a generic countdown. The transferable lesson is that loss aversion and audience-native voice, applied at the inbox layer, lift opens before the body copy ever gets a chance. We are now carrying that framing into the flows still on generic urgency.

narrative.html: Flows earned more per email this month. Revenue per email delivered rose to 0.740 AUD from 0.726, so the automations converted each send harder even as total flow revenue settled to 634,548 AUD (-4.9%). The dip is volume, not efficiency.

Flows held 28.6% of total store revenue. On a store that turned over 2,217,343 AUD across all orders, more than a quarter came through the automations we run. That share sits in line with the strong months of the past year rather than being a one-off spike.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. At 0.740 AUD per email, flows earned 9.2x what campaigns did per send, and they drove 71% of email revenue this month. Campaigns are the second lever we also run: 19 sends this month, working the broadcast demand that flows cannot reach on their own.

Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes came in at 0.627% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.035%, well inside safe territory. That protects inbox placement, which is what keeps the per-email numbers above holding up.

monthly.title_sub: Flows held 28.6% of total store revenue and earned more per email than last month, even as monthly flow revenue eased slightly.
